newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan computer output up 28 percent a year in '92-95.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan computer output up 28 percent a year in '92-95.

text.p: Taiwan's computer industry grew an average 28 percent a year from 1992 to 1995, hitting a production value of US$19.7 billion in 1995 to rank as the world's third largest, official statistics showed on Thursday.
Taiwan's 1995 output was eclipsed only by the U.S. computer sector's $65.1 billion output and Japan's $63.6 billion output, said the Directorate General of Budget, Accounting and Statistics.

Three key products -- computer monitors, portable computers and desktop computers -- accounted for 75.6 percent of the 1995 production value and were mainly for export to the United States and Europe, the statement said.

To trim production costs and gain preferential tariff treatments, Taiwan manufacturers in recent years have increased overseas production, mainly in the assembly of labour-intensive low-end products, it said.
Seventy-two percent of the 1995 output was made in Taiwan firms' overseas plants, down from 79.4 percent in 1994, 85.1 percent in 1993, and 89.6 percent in 1992, it said.

In 1995, Taiwan computer goods held more than 50 percent of global market share in five categories -- pointing devices or mouses (72 percent), motherboards (65 percent), keyboards (65 percent), image scanners (64 percent) and monitors (57 percent).
Taiwan's global market share of motherboards slipped from 80 percent a year earlier mainly because U.S. giant Intel Corp began making motherboards then, the statement said.

The semi-official Institute for Information Industry had forecast Taiwan's total computer or information product output in 1996 would rise 25 percent to $24.6 billion from $19.7 billion in 1995, it said.
